tool.name: GBIFSpeciesOccurrences

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/data-tools/gbif-species-occurrences.html
Gets species occurrence records from the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF.org) and writes them as a point feature class, for the species or groups, study area, dates and kinds of record you choose. The records are fetched directly (up to 100,000), or through a GBIF download that GBIF prepares under your free account and that carries a DOI to cite, or from a download that already exists. This is the scripting form of the GBIF Species Occurrences window on the ribbon, which finds species by common name, lists the species and sources of an area, shows photographs, and then runs this tool, so that every run of the window is recorded in the Geoprocessing History. Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
The window or the tool. The GBIF Species Occurrences window (Data Tools group, Online Data) is the easier way to choose what to get: it searches names as you type, counts the matching records, and lists the species and the sources in an area before anything is fetched. Its last step runs this tool. To automate a request, make it once in the window, then right-click its entry in the Geoprocessing History and choose Copy Python Command.
Three ways to get the records: • Fetch directly -- quick, no account needed, at most 100,000 records. GBIF issues no DOI for records fetched this way. • Request a GBIF download -- any number of records. GBIF prepares a file under your account and gives it a DOI and a citation. The tool waits for the file, fetches it, writes the records, and keeps the original zip file in a folder named Data_Downloads in the project folder (beside the output geodatabase when the tool runs outside a project), under the same name as the output feature class. • Load an existing GBIF download -- a download that is already on GBIF or already on disk, named by its GBIF key or by the path of its zip file. Nothing new is requested from GBIF.
The GBIF account. A download request needs your GBIF account. The tool has no user name or password parameter. It reads the sign-in that the GBIF Species Occurrences window keeps in Windows Credential Manager under your own Windows login (the entry JennessWildlifeTools.GBIF), so sign in once in the window with Remember checked. On a computer with no such entry, the environment variables GBIF_USER and GBIF_PWD are read instead. The password is never written to a message, a file, the Geoprocessing History or a copied Python command. The messages name the account the request was made on.
Waiting for GBIF. GBIF does not say how long a download will take. The tool asks GBIF for the state of the request every fifteen seconds and stops with an error if GBIF reports that the request failed or was cancelled, or when the longest wait passes. The messages give the download key as soon as GBIF accepts the request; a request that is still running when the longest wait passes stays on the account, and can be loaded later with the method Load an existing GBIF download and that key. Cancelling the tool while it waits cancels the request at GBIF as well. The key, the DOI and the path of the zip file are also derived outputs of the tool, for scripts.
Species or groups. Give scientific names, GBIF taxon keys, or a name followed by its key in brackets, separated by semicolons: Antilocapra americana; 2440901; Odocoileus hemionus (2440974). A key includes every taxon below it and its synonyms. A name is matched against the GBIF backbone taxonomy, and the messages say what each entry was read as; a name GBIF cannot place stops the tool before anything is fetched. Common names are not accepted here; the window finds the scientific name and key from a common name.
Study area. A polygon layer (its selection and definition query are honored; polygons that overlap or adjoin are merged) or a rectangle. A study area with more than 10,000 vertices is too detailed for GBIF's download service, so for a download the tool simplifies the study area first (to its convex hull), downloads the records inside that simpler shape, and then clips them to the true study area when they are written. A direct fetch is not affected.
Records without coordinates. Many records name a country, a state or a county but carry no coordinates. With that option checked they are written as rows that have no point. A study area polygon cannot limit them, so give a country or a state or province as well.
Loading an existing download. The species, dates and kinds of record were applied by GBIF when the download was made, and those parameters are not applied again. A study area given here does cut the records, and the option for records without coordinates applies.
The output. A point feature class in WGS 84 inside a file geodatabase, with the same 48 fields whichever way the records came. A record that has a photograph carries the web address of its first photograph in the photoURL field (empty for a download in GBIF's Simple format, which does not carry it). A record at latitude 0, longitude 0 is never written as a point. The feature class's metadata records the choices, the date, the DOI and citation of a download, and the licenses of the records. An existing feature class of the same name is replaced when geoprocessing is allowed to overwrite outputs.
Checking the data. GBIF data is not reviewed record by record. Check the locality, the basis of record and the coordinate uncertainty of any record that matters, and of any point far outside a species' known range.

param.name: taxa
param.displayname: Species or groups (scientific names or GBIF taxon keys, separated by semicolons)

dialogReference.para: Scientific names, GBIF taxon keys, or a name followed by its key in brackets, separated by semicolons, for example Antilocapra americana; 2440901; Odocoileus hemionus (2440974). A key includes every taxon below it and its synonyms. Empty means every species, which needs a study area or a country.
A polygon layer or feature class. A layer's selection and definition query are honored. Overlapping or adjoining polygons are merged.

param.name: extent
param.displayname: Or a rectangle as the study area

dialogReference.para: A rectangle to use as the study area when no polygon layer is given. Numbers typed without a coordinate system are read as degrees of longitude and latitude (west, south, east, north).
The two-letter ISO code of a country or area, such as US, CA or MX.

param.name: state_province
param.displayname: State or province (exactly as the records spell it, such as Arizona)

dialogReference.para: GBIF matches this text letter for letter: Arizona finds records, arizona and AZ do not. The window lists the spellings the records use.

param.name: include_no_coordinates
param.displayname: Also get records that have no coordinates

dialogReference.para: Checked, records without coordinates are written as rows that have no point. A study area polygon cannot limit them, so give a country or a state or province as well.
The earliest year to get. Empty for no limit.
The latest year to get. Empty for no limit.
The months to get, as numbers 1 to 12. Empty for all months.

bulletList.bullet_item: Observations: a person or an instrument recorded the organism in the field.
Museum and herbarium specimens: preserved specimens in collections. A specimen can come from a captive animal or a cultivated plant.
Material samples: samples such as tissue, soil or water, and specimens cited in publications.
Zoos and gardens: living organisms in captivity or cultivation.

dialogReference.para: The first three are chosen by default. Empty, or all five, gets every kind.

param.name: exclude_location_problems
param.displayname: Leave out records whose location GBIF flags as a problem

dialogReference.para: GBIF checks every record's coordinates (zero coordinates, wrong country, swapped latitude and longitude and more). Checked, the records that failed those checks are left out.

param.name: exclude_centroids
param.displayname: Leave out records placed at the center of a country or region

dialogReference.para: Some records have no real coordinates and were given the center point of their country, state or province instead. GBIF marks records within 5 kilometers of such a center point; checked, they are left out.
Checked, records of a species being looked for and not found are left out.

param.name: exclude_noncommercial
param.displayname: Leave out records licensed for non-commercial use only (CC BY-NC)

dialogReference.para: Every GBIF record carries one of three licenses: CC0 (no restriction), CC BY (credit required) or CC BY-NC (credit required, non-commercial use only). Check this if your work is commercial.
Checked, only records that carry a still image are returned.
Keeps only records whose stated coordinate uncertainty is at most this many meters. Records that state no uncertainty at all are left out too, so use this with care. Empty for no limit.

param.name: excluded_sources
param.displayname: Sources to leave out (GBIF dataset keys, separated by semicolons)

dialogReference.para: GBIF dataset keys of sources whose records are not wanted. The window's Sources tab lists the sources of a request with their keys, and the datasetKey field of an output carries them.

bulletList.bullet_item: Fetch directly: quick, no account needed, at most 100,000 records, no DOI.
Request a GBIF download: any number of records, a DOI and a citation; needs the GBIF sign-in kept by the GBIF Species Occurrences window.
Load an existing GBIF download: the download named in the next parameter; nothing new is requested.

param.name: existing_download
param.displayname: Existing download (its GBIF key, or the path of its zip file)

dialogReference.para: For the method Load an existing GBIF download: the download's GBIF key, such as 0012345-260101123456789 (the tool prints it when it requests a download, and GBIF.org shows it on the download's page), or the full path of a GBIF download zip file on disk. A download GBIF is still preparing is waited for.

param.name: max_wait_minutes
param.displayname: Longest wait for GBIF to prepare a download (minutes)

dialogReference.para: How long to wait for GBIF before stopping with an error that names the download key. The request keeps running at GBIF and can be loaded later with that key. The default is 60 minutes.

param.name: out_features
param.displayname: Output point feature class (in a file geodatabase)

dialogReference.para: The point feature class to create, directly inside a file geodatabase (not in a feature dataset). The field names are too long for a shapefile.
The key of the GBIF download the records came from; empty for a direct fetch.
The DOI GBIF gave the download; empty for a direct fetch.
The path of the download's zip file on disk; empty for a direct fetch.

scriptExample.title: Fetch directly (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Pronghorn records inside a study area, fetched directly.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.jenness.GBIFSpeciesOccurrences( taxa="Antilocapra americana (2440902)", study_area=r"D:\data\study.gdb\Forest_Boundary", year_from=2000, method="Fetch directly", out_features=r"D:\data\study.gdb\Pronghorn_GBIF")

scriptExample.title: Request a download, then load the same download again later
scriptExample.para: The first run asks GBIF for a download and returns its key; a later run loads that same download, with the same DOI, without a new request.
scriptExample.code:
import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path result = arcpy.jenness.GBIFSpeciesOccurrences( taxa="Antilocapra americana (2440902)", country="US", state_province="Arizona", method="Request a GBIF download", max_wait_minutes=120, out_features=r"D:\data\study.gdb\Pronghorn_Arizona") key = result.getOutput(1) # the GBIF download key doi = result.getOutput(2)
arcpy.jenness.GBIFSpeciesOccurrences( method="Load an existing GBIF download", existing_download=key, out_features=r"D:\data\study.gdb\Pronghorn_Arizona_again")
